sentences.text: Maya locked in 7.62%.
sentences.spoken: Maya locked in seven point six two percent.

sentences.text: This week's average: 7.03%.
sentences.spoken: This week's average, seven point zero three percent.

sentences.text: Refinancing costs $5,124.
sentences.spoken: Refinancing costs five thousand, one hundred twenty-four dollars.

sentences.text: So when does that money come back?
sentences.spoken: So... when does that money... come back?

sentences.text: This is a lab for money decisions: we run the numbers on public data, and show every assumption.
sentences.spoken: This is a lab for money decisions... we run the numbers on public data... and show every assumption.

sentences.text: US only. The rates here are history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: U.S. only. The rates here are history... not a forecast.

sentences.text: By the end, you will see the exact rate drop that pays back a refinance like Maya's within 36 months, and how every rate drop since 1971 actually played out.
sentences.spoken: By the end... you will see the exact rate drop that pays back a refinance like Maya's within thirty-six months... and how every rate drop since nineteen seventy-one actually played out.

sentences.text: She borrowed $375,000 in October 2023, the month the 30-year rate peaked.
sentences.spoken: She borrowed three hundred seventy-five thousand dollars in October twenty twenty-three... the month the thirty-year rate peaked.

sentences.text: And if your own rate starts with a 7, the question is yours as well.
sentences.spoken: And if your own rate starts with a seven... the question is yours as well.

sentences.text: First: is Maya's bill unusual?
sentences.spoken: First... is Maya's bill unusual?

sentences.text: No. In 2025, the median closing cost on a rate-and-term refinance was $5,124.
sentences.spoken: No. In twenty twenty-five... the median closing cost on a rate-and-term refinance was five thousand one hundred twenty-four dollars.

sentences.text: Lenders must report every mortgage they make, and since 2018, the total loan costs of each one.
sentences.spoken: Lenders must report every mortgage they make... and since twenty eighteen... the total loan costs of each one.

sentences.text: That is the middle of 488,241 such loans that lenders reported under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act.
sentences.spoken: That is the middle of four hundred eighty-eight thousand two hundred forty-one such loans that lenders reported under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act.

sentences.text: Half of those borrowers paid between $3,443 and $8,270.
sentences.spoken: Half of those borrowers paid between three thousand four hundred forty-three dollars... and eight thousand two hundred seventy dollars.

sentences.text: The bill is the closing costs: origination charges, discount points, the appraisal, title insurance, and the rest.
sentences.spoken: The bill is the closing costs... origination charges... discount points... the appraisal... title insurance... and the rest.

sentences.text: But that bill barely grows with the loan, so it lands much harder on some borrowers than on others.
sentences.spoken: But that bill barely grows with the loan... so it lands much harder on some borrowers than on others.

sentences.text: Take Dan, who borrowed $115,000 in the same month, at the same rate.
sentences.spoken: Take Dan... who borrowed one hundred fifteen thousand dollars in the same month... at the same rate.

sentences.text: On loans under $150,000, the median bill was 3.4% of the amount borrowed.
sentences.spoken: On loans under one hundred fifty thousand dollars... the median bill was three point four percent of the amount borrowed.

sentences.text: For Dan, that is $3,667: fewer dollars than Maya, but a far larger share of his loan.
sentences.spoken: For Dan... that is three thousand six hundred sixty-seven dollars... fewer dollars than Maya... but a far larger share of his loan.

sentences.text: Priya borrowed $1,005,000.
sentences.spoken: Priya borrowed one million five thousand dollars.

sentences.text: On loans of $750,000 and more, the bill was 0.5%.
sentences.spoken: On loans of seven hundred fifty thousand dollars and more... the bill was zero point five percent.

sentences.text: For Priya, that is $5,034: about Maya's bill, on a loan nearly three times the size.
sentences.spoken: For Priya... that is five thousand thirty-four dollars... about Maya's bill... on a loan nearly three times the size.

sentences.text: What the bill buys is a lower payment. At today's rate, Maya's payment falls by $221 a month.
sentences.spoken: What the bill buys is a lower payment. At today's rate... Maya's payment falls by two hundred twenty-one dollars a month.

sentences.text: Divide the bill by that saving, and you get the answer most calculators give: 24 months.
sentences.spoken: Divide the bill by that saving... and you get the answer most calculators give... twenty-four months.

sentences.text: By that count, the refinance has paid for itself. Or has it?
sentences.spoken: By that count... the refinance has paid for itself. Or has it?

sentences.text: Here is what that division leaves out.
sentences.spoken: Here is what that division leaves out.

sentences.text: Maya's old loan already has 35 payments behind it.
sentences.spoken: Maya's old loan already has thirty-five payments behind it.

sentences.text: A refinance starts a fresh 30 years, so the new loan pays the balance down more slowly than the old one would have.
sentences.spoken: A refinance starts a fresh thirty years... so the new loan pays the balance down more slowly than the old one would have.

sentences.text: Early payments are mostly interest. Maya's old loan was just starting to pay down real principal, and the new one starts that schedule over.
sentences.spoken: Early payments are mostly interest. Maya's old loan was just starting to pay down real principal... and the new one starts that schedule over.

sentences.text: So count what she still owes on each loan, month by month.
sentences.spoken: So count what she still owes on each loan... month by month.

sentences.text: After 24 months, the new loan leaves her owing $1,133 more than the old one would have.
sentences.spoken: After twenty-four months... the new loan leaves her owing one thousand one hundred thirty-three dollars more than the old one would have.

sentences.text: So, counting what she still owes, break-even is not 24 months. It is 30.
sentences.spoken: So... counting what she still owes... break-even is not twenty-four months. It is thirty.

sentences.text: Most calculators stop at the monthly saving. The balance keeps the score for longer.
sentences.spoken: Most calculators stop at the monthly saving. The balance keeps the score for longer.

sentences.text: The smaller the cut, the bigger that gap.
sentences.spoken: The smaller the cut... the bigger that gap.

sentences.text: At a cut of 0.25 points, the division would promise 38 months.
sentences.spoken: At a cut of zero point two five points... the division would promise thirty-eight months.

sentences.text: Counting the balance, Maya never catches up before her old loan would have been paid off.
sentences.spoken: Counting the balance... Maya never catches up before her old loan would have been paid off.

sentences.text: Below 0.5 points, the fresh start can swallow the savings entirely.
sentences.spoken: Below zero point five points... the fresh start can swallow the savings entirely.

sentences.text: At a cut of 1 point, the two answers nearly meet.
sentences.spoken: At a cut of one point... the two answers nearly meet.

sentences.text: The division says 16 months; the balance says 18.
sentences.spoken: The division says sixteen months... the balance says eighteen.

sentences.text: Now Dan. At today's rate, his payment falls by only $68 a month.
sentences.spoken: Now Dan. At today's rate... his payment falls by only sixty-eight dollars a month.

sentences.text: The division says 55 months. Counting what he still owes, it is 75.
sentences.spoken: The division says fifty-five months. Counting what he still owes... it is seventy-five.

sentences.text: If Dan sells after 3 years, the refinance leaves him $1,777 behind.
sentences.spoken: If Dan sells after three years... the refinance leaves him one thousand seven hundred seventy-seven dollars behind.

sentences.text: After 7 years, he is only $386 ahead.
sentences.spoken: After seven years... he is only three hundred eighty-six dollars ahead.

sentences.text: Priya saves $593 a month, and is even after 11 months.
sentences.spoken: Priya saves five hundred ninety-three dollars a month... and is even after eleven months.

sentences.text: If she sells after 3 years, she is $11,482 ahead; after 7, $30,387.
sentences.spoken: If she sells after three years... she is eleven thousand four hundred eighty-two dollars ahead... after seven... thirty thousand three hundred eighty-seven dollars.

sentences.text: And Maya, the middle case: $1,039 ahead after 3 years, $8,093 after 7.
sentences.spoken: And Maya... the middle case... one thousand thirty-nine dollars ahead after three years... eight thousand ninety-three dollars after seven.

sentences.text: Put another way: a house sold before the break-even month turns the refinance into a loss, and one kept past it turns it into a gain.
sentences.spoken: Put another way... a house sold before the break-even month turns the refinance into a loss... and one kept past it turns it into a gain.

sentences.text: Same rate, same month. The answer depends on the size of the loan, how old it is, and how long the house is kept.
sentences.spoken: Same rate... same month. The answer depends on the size of the loan... how old it is... and how long the house is kept.

sentences.text: The division also assumes today's rate is the last one. What happened in the real drops?
sentences.spoken: The division also assumes today's rate is the last one. What happened... in the real drops?

sentences.text: We found every fall of at least 1 point in the 30-year rate since 1971: 13 of them.
sentences.spoken: We found every fall of at least one point in the thirty-year rate since nineteen seventy-one... thirteen of them.

sentences.text: In each, someone like Maya borrows at the peak and refinances in the first month the rate is 1 point lower.
sentences.spoken: In each... someone like Maya borrows at the peak and refinances in the first month the rate is one point lower.

sentences.text: Closing costs use each year's median share; before 2018, lenders did not report them, so a fixed share is used and marked illustrative.
sentences.spoken: Closing costs use each year's median share... before twenty eighteen... lenders did not report them... so a fixed share is used and marked illustrative.

sentences.text: Counting what was still owed, break-even took between 10 and 20 months.
sentences.spoken: Counting what was still owed... break-even took between ten and twenty months.

sentences.text: The simple division would have said between 10 and 21.
sentences.spoken: The simple division would have said between ten and twenty-one.

sentences.text: Nearly the same, because those loans were only months old when the rate fell, so the fresh start cost them little. Maya's loan is 35 payments old.
sentences.spoken: Nearly the same... because those loans were only months old when the rate fell... so the fresh start cost them little. Maya's loan is thirty-five payments old.

sentences.text: The biggest fall began after the peak of 18.63% in 1981.
sentences.spoken: The biggest fall began... after the peak of eighteen point six three percent in nineteen eighty-one.

sentences.text: A refinance 2 months later paid back in 13 months, and the rate kept falling.
sentences.spoken: A refinance two months later paid back in thirteen months... and the rate kept falling.

sentences.text: For Priya's loan size, every one of those drops paid back within 6 months.
sentences.spoken: For Priya's loan size... every one of those drops paid back within six months.

sentences.text: For a loan like Dan's, with the bill a bigger share, the same drops took between 18 and 39 months.
sentences.spoken: For a loan like Dan's... with the bill a bigger share... the same drops took between eighteen and thirty-nine months.

sentences.text: But in 3 of those drops, the rate fell another 1 point before the first refinance had paid for itself.
sentences.spoken: But in three of those drops... the rate fell another one point before the first refinance had paid for itself.

sentences.text: Those borrowers met the same question twice, and a second refinance starts a new clock with a new bill.
sentences.spoken: Those borrowers met the same question twice... and a second refinance starts a new clock with a new bill.

sentences.text: In the drop that began in July 1984, the refinance came in November 1984.
sentences.spoken: In the drop that began in July nineteen eighty-four... the refinance came in November nineteen eighty-four.

sentences.text: It needed 19 months to pay back, and the next drop of 1 point came 7 months later.
sentences.spoken: It needed nineteen months to pay back... and the next drop of one point came seven months later.

sentences.text: In the other 10, the first refinance was the one that mattered.
sentences.spoken: In the other ten... the first refinance was the one that mattered.

sentences.text: Maya's own drop began in October 2023. A cut of 1 point first arrived in August 2024.
sentences.spoken: Maya's own drop began... in October twenty twenty-three. A cut of one point first arrived in August twenty twenty-four.

sentences.text: Refinancing then would have paid back in 19 months.
sentences.spoken: Refinancing then would have paid back in nineteen months.

sentences.text: So, how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?
sentences.spoken: So... how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?

sentences.text: For a loan like Maya's, counting what is still owed, a cut of 0.5 points pays it back within 36 months.
sentences.spoken: For a loan like Maya's... counting what is still owed... a cut of zero point five points pays it back within thirty-six months.

sentences.text: Dan would need 1.12 points. Priya, 0.2.
sentences.spoken: Dan would need one point one two points. Priya... zero point two.

sentences.text: Today's cut is 0.59 points. For Maya, that means ahead after 30 months, and behind if the house is sold before then.
sentences.spoken: Today's cut is zero point five nine points. For Maya... that means ahead after thirty months... and behind if the house is sold before then.

sentences.text: That answer has limits. It leaves out taxes and any return on the cash, and it assumes the bill is paid up front, not added to the loan.
sentences.spoken: That answer has limits. It leaves out taxes and any return on the cash... and it assumes the bill is paid up front... not added to the loan.

sentences.text: It uses medians: half of borrowers paid more than $5,124, and an offered rate can differ from the survey average.
sentences.spoken: It uses medians... half of borrowers paid more than five thousand one hundred twenty-four dollars... and an offered rate can differ from the survey average.

sentences.text: And it is history, not a forecast: nothing here says where rates go next.
sentences.spoken: And it is history... not a forecast... nothing here says where rates go next.

sentences.text: What history does show is the shape of the trade: a known bill up front, against savings and a balance that settle month by month.
sentences.spoken: What history does show is the shape of the trade... a known bill up front... against savings and a balance that settle month by month.

sentences.text: Method. Rates are Freddie Mac's weekly survey via FRED, checked against the Optimal Blue index since 2017.
sentences.spoken: Method. Rates are Freddie Mac's weekly survey via Fred... checked against the Optimal Blue index since twenty seventeen.

sentences.text: A drop counts when the monthly average falls at least 1 point from a peak before rising 1 point from its low.
sentences.spoken: A drop counts when the monthly average falls at least one point... from a peak before rising one point from its low.

sentences.text: Costs are HMDA loan-level data from 2018 to 2025: originated refinances, first lien, 30-year term.
sentences.spoken: Costs are H.M.D.A. loan-level data from twenty eighteen to twenty twenty-five... originated refinances... first lien... thirty-year term.

sentences.text: Maya, Dan and Priya are illustrative: each one's loan and bill are the medians for that loan size.
sentences.spoken: Maya... Dan and Priya are illustrative... each one's loan and bill are the medians for that loan size.

sentences.text: Break-even counts payment savings plus the difference in balance still owed. Closing costs paid in cash; no taxes. Every figure is listed in the description.
sentences.spoken: Break-even counts payment savings plus the difference in balance still owed. Closing costs paid in cash... no taxes. Every figure is listed in the description.

sentences.text: A small cut needs a long stay. A small loan needs a bigger cut. And a young loan loses less to the fresh start.
sentences.spoken: A small cut needs a long stay... A small loan needs a bigger cut... And a young loan... loses less to the fresh start.

sentences.text: If the rate on your own statement starts with a 7, the same three questions apply: how big the cut, how old the loan, and how long the stay.
sentences.spoken: If the rate on your own statement starts with a seven... the same three questions apply... how big the cut... how old the loan... and how long the stay.

sentences.text: The monthly saving is only half of the answer. The other half, just as real, is what is still owed.
sentences.spoken: The monthly saving is only half of the answer. The other half... just as real... is what is still owed.

sentences.text: The sources are linked in the description, and the next decision is already on the bench.
sentences.spoken: The sources are linked in the description... and the next decision is already on the bench.
